US Sports Market Expansion: David Hampian on Rugby, NRL, and Broadcast Strategy

David Hampian provides expert analysis to the Australian Financial Review on the challenges facing international sports leagues entering the US market, drawing on his experience launching Hard Rock Bet and leading Twitch's expansion into sports broadcasting.

Topic Sports Marketing & US Market Entry
Author Jessica Gardner
David's Role Marketing consultant and US sports market expert who launched Hard Rock Bet and led Twitch's expansion into sports broadcasting

Context

The Australian Financial Review — Australia’s leading business and financial publication — consulted David Hampian as a US sports marketing expert for a feature analyzing the competitive dynamics between rugby union and rugby league (NRL) in the American market. Hampian’s commentary draws on his direct experience launching Hard Rock Bet and leading Twitch’s expansion into sports content, giving him a practitioner’s view of what it takes for a sports property to gain traction in the world’s most competitive entertainment market.

Why This Matters

The US sports market represents the largest revenue opportunity for international leagues — but also the highest barrier to entry. With rugby union securing broadcast deals, college programs, and growing grassroots participation, the NRL faces a strategic challenge that’s as much about marketing and content infrastructure as it is about the sport itself. Hampian’s analysis frames this as a marketing and distribution problem, not just a competition for fans.

David Hampian’s Expertise

Hampian brings hands-on experience in US sports market entry and sports betting launch strategy. His work launching Hard Rock Bet gave him deep exposure to the intersection of sports media, betting, and fan engagement. His leadership of Twitch’s expansion into sports broadcasting provided insight into how digital-first platforms can create year-round audience engagement — a capability he argues is essential for any international league seeking US relevance.

Key Themes

  • US market entry strategy: Why international sports leagues struggle with the “awareness-to-habit” gap in American markets
  • Content-first approach: How the English Premier League’s content and broadcast strategy offers a playbook for sustained US growth
  • Year-round engagement: Why seasonal competition models fail in the US without 365-day content infrastructure
  • Broadcast and betting convergence: How the intersection of media rights, sports betting, and digital platforms shapes the competitive landscape for emerging sports in America
  • The NRL’s strategic gap: Specific challenges facing the National Rugby League in building US audience infrastructure

About David Hampian

David Hampian is the Managing Director of Field Vision, a San Francisco-based strategic marketing consultancy. With over 15 years of experience spanning the music, sports, entertainment, and technology industries, Hampian has held leadership roles at Pandora, Twitch, Amazon Music, and Hard Rock Digital. He specializes in integrated marketing strategy, go-to-market execution, and brand building for high-growth companies.

As a fractional CMO and marketing consultant, Hampian works with growth-stage companies and enterprise organizations to build marketing infrastructure that drives measurable business outcomes. His work has been featured in the Australian Financial Review, Covers, Daily Express, and Birch.
